activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
fact: Singing a song while you scrub helps you keep washing long enough.
story:
Grace sat in the big chair at the dentist. She had just picked a sticker. Now it was time for a snack. But first, the dentist said, "Time to wash your hands, Grace."

Grace ran to the little sink. She pumped the soap. She rubbed her hands twice. Then she stopped. "Is that long enough?" she asked.

The dentist shook her head. "Sing the happy birthday song while you scrub," she said. "Singing a song while you scrub helps you keep washing long enough."

Grace began to sing. "Happy birthday to you..." She scrubbed and scrubbed. The soap turned fuzzy and white on her hands. Little bubbles tried to hide between her fingers. She found them all.

She finished the song. Then she rinsed. The water felt cool, like ice on her fingers. Where had all the bubbles gone? Down the drain, swish!

Grace looked at her hands. They were clean and shiny. "The song made me wash a long time," she said.

"That's right," said the dentist. She held out a small cracker. Grace took it with her clean hands and took a big bite.

"My hands smell like soap," Grace said. She waved her hands in the air. "Goodbye, germs! Go hide somewhere else!"

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
fact: Children ask a grown-up before using a tablet.
story:
Ibrahim ran to Maya's house. Maya had a tablet on the table. It was flat and shiny and blue. "Can we use the tablet?" Ibrahim asked Maya's grandpa.

"Yes, you may," said Grandpa. "Children ask a grown-up first. Good asking!" Grandpa tapped the button. The screen lit up like a little window. "Now you try," he said. Ibrahim pressed the button. The light came on! He laughed. His finger made the light.

"Open the drawing app," said Maya. Ibrahim tapped the green square. It opened with a pop. He drew a big sun. He drew a purple cat. The cat had three legs. "Silly cat!" said Maya. They laughed so hard the table shook.

Then the sun went down in the sky. Time to go home. Ibrahim pressed the button. The screen went dark. He slid the tablet into its soft case. "I put it away," he said. "Bye bye, purple cat." Grandpa smiled and waved. "Come learn more tomorrow," he called. "I will bring the cat a fourth leg!"

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
fact: If you get lost in a store, tell a store worker you can't find your grown-up.
story:
Jayden was at home with Mom. "We need a present for Grandma," Mom said. They put on shoes and went to the store.

The store was big and bright. Jayden held Mom's hand. He saw a thin ribbon. He saw a candle. He did not touch it. Mom said, "Only grown-ups touch candles." There was tea in a pot. Steam rose up. "That is hot," Mom said. Jayden looked with his eyes only.

Then Jayden saw a teddy bear. It was soft and brown. He let go of Mom's hand. He hugged the bear. When he looked up, Mom was not there. Jayden felt worried. He saw a lady at the checkout. She had a kind face. "I can't find my grown-up," Jayden said. "Let's find your mom," the lady said. She stood with him and called out.

Mom came fast. She hugged Jayden tight. "You told the store lady. That was good," Mom said. They bought the teddy bear for Grandma. At home, Grandma opened her present. She smiled and smiled. The ice cream cake began to melt, so everyone ate fast. Jayden licked his spoon. "Cold!" he said. Grandma laughed and held his hand.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: In a pretend shop, one person can be the shopkeeper and another can be the shopper.
story:
Joshua went to his friend Mia's house. Mia had set up a little shop. It had a table and a door made from a cardboard box.

"I am the shopkeeper," said Mia. She stood behind the table. "You be the shopper."

Joshua did not know what to do. He just stood there. Mia waited. She did not pick anything for him.

Then Joshua picked up a toy apple. He gave Mia a button for money. Mia put the button in a cup. "Thank you," she said.

The shop had a little pot, too. Joshua asked, "Can I stir the pot?" Mia said yes. He stirred and stirred with a wooden spoon. Round and round went the soup.

After that, Joshua wanted a turn behind the table. They swapped. Now Mia was the shopper. Joshua waited for her to choose. She chose a toy banana. She gave him a leaf for money.

Then came a surprise. The leaf had a tiny ladybug on it. The ladybug crawled onto Joshua's hand. "Look!" he said.

They played shop all morning. The baby doll got tired and slept in a shoe box bed. Joshua stirred more soup. The door of the shop went open and shut, open and shut.

Then Joshua held out his hand. "Hello, ladybug," he said. "Do you want one apple?"

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
fact: A grown-up plugs the charger into the wall.
story:
Charlotte was at her friend Mia's house. Mia had a tablet. Charlotte wanted to draw on it. She tapped the screen. The screen stayed dark. She tapped it again. Still dark.

Mia's mom came over. "Here is the charger," she said. "I will plug it into the wall." Charlotte watched. The charger went into the wall plug. The cord went into the tablet. A little picture came on the screen.

"Now you can try," said Mia's mom. Charlotte pressed the round button. The screen lit up. She had made that happen. She tapped the drawing app. She drew a big green hill. She drew a yellow sun on top. "I hear the sun," said Mia, laughing at the silly idea. Charlotte laughed too.

Soon the tablet said it was tired. Charlotte drew one last picture. It was a small cat. Then she gave the tablet to Mia's mom. "All done," said Charlotte. The tablet went on the shelf, nice and safe.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
fact: Shirts, socks and hats are all clothes.
story:
Sarah ran into the library. Storytime was starting soon! There was a big box on the rug. "A dress-up box!" said Miss Kim.

Sarah looked inside. She saw a shirt. She saw a hat. She saw a sock. She put on the big hat. It fell over her eyes. "Too big!" she laughed. Then she found a toy bunny with rough fur. She could bend its soft ears.

Sarah dropped the sock on the floor. Then she picked it up. She put it with the toy bunny. Bunny had fur. Socks were soft too! She laughed at her own silly mix-up and moved the sock to the shirt and the hat.

"Shirts, socks and hats are all clothes," said Miss Kim. "You got it!" Sarah looked at the picture on her shirt. A cat was on it. "My shirt has an animal!" she said. Miss Kim clapped, and storytime began.

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
fact: Tracing over dotted letters is one way to practice making letter shapes.
story:
Max sat at Grandma's kitchen table. He wanted to write his name, Max. But the pencil wiggled in his hand. His letters came out like wiggly worms. "Mine looks funny," Max said.

Grandma sat down next to him. "Here is a paper for you," she said. On the paper was the letter M. But it was not a solid letter. It was made of little dots. Max tapped one dot with his finger. "Try tracing over them," said Grandma.

Max put his pencil on the first dot. He drew a line to the next dot. Then the next one, and the next one. His pencil tip hopped from dot to dot, like feet on stones. Would the dots turn into a letter? Max kept going. The dots made a big M!

Max traced the a next. Then the x. He wrote his whole name! He watched the pencil marks dry. Then he ran to show his big brother. "Look, Ben! It says Max!" Ben clapped. Max sat back down at the table. "Can I trace dots again?" he asked. Grandma was already drawing more.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: Saying "Let's pretend" tells your friends a game is starting.
story:
Nicholas was at Grandma's house. He wanted to play with his cousin Mia. But Mia sat with her bear and did not look up. Nicholas tried to hand her a block. Mia did not take it. He tried to sit next to her. She just hugged her bear.

"What do you like to play?" Nicholas asked. "House," said Mia. "How do we start?" he asked. Mia smiled big. "Just say let's pretend," she said. "Let's pretend we have a house!" said Nicholas. Mia jumped up. Now the game began!

Mia made the bear a bed from a box. Nicholas fed the bear a pretend bottle. The bear got grumpy and cried. "He needs a hug," said Mia. Nicholas counted one, two, three pats. The bear went to sleep. "Let's pretend the bear is a baby dog," said Nicholas. Mia laughed. "Woof, woof," she said.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: Dress-up clothes help you pretend to be someone else.
story:
Willow wanted to play firefighter at school. But her friend Sam said, "You can't be a firefighter. You are just Willow."

Willow frowned. Then she saw the dress-up box. She pulled out a big red hat. She put it on her head. "Look at me!" she said. "I am a firefighter now!"

Sam's eyes went wide. "A firefighter!" he said. "Help! My teddy bear is stuck up high!"

Willow ran over on her fast feet. She stood on her tiptoes. She reached up with both hands. She grabbed the teddy bear. "I got him!" she said. She held him close and patted his head. "There, there. You are safe now."

Sam clapped. "Thank you, firefighter!" Willow's hat stayed on her head. She felt very awake and very proud. "Firefighters keep teddy bears safe," she said.

Then Sam dug in the box too. He found a shiny silver hat. He put it on. "Now I am a firefighter too!" he said.

Two firefighters ran off to find the next teddy bear in trouble.

activity: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
knowledge_domain: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
fact: Playing with one toy together, like building one tower side by side, is another way to share.
story:
Gianna saw the blocks at the party. A boy named Sam grabbed them first. Gianna wanted them too. Her hand reached out, but she stopped.

"Can I have a turn?" she asked.

"You can have them next," said Sam.

Gianna waited. It was hard to wait. She watched Sam stack one block. Then another. The tower was thin and wobbly.

"Is waiting done yet?" she asked herself. "Not yet. I can wait a little more."

Sam looked at her sad face. "Do you want to help me?" he asked.

Gianna nodded. "We can build one big tower together," said Sam.

Gianna put a red block on top. Sam put a blue one. Back and forth they went. The tower grew tall.

"Wow," said Gianna. "One tower. Two kids. We both played!"

"Want to knock it down?" asked Sam.

They counted, "One, two, three!" and pushed it over together. The blocks went crash, and they both laughed and laughed.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
fact: Seeds need water to start growing, and a sprout does not come up right away.
story:
Olivia went to the garden center with Gran. The sun was bright. "The sun can burn your nose," said Gran. So Olivia wore her big hat.

A truck beeped outside. It was very loud. Olivia held Gran's hand. Then it was quiet again.

Olivia picked little seeds. They were tiny and hard. They felt like small beads in her palm. They smelled like dirt. She found a pot and some brown soil. She made three little holes. She dropped the seeds in. She patted the soil down on top.

Gran checked the weather on her phone. "No rain today," she said. "The seeds need water to start growing." Olivia filled her small watering can. She tipped it over the pot. The soil turned dark and damp.

The next morning, Olivia ran to the pot. She saw only dirt. No sprout. Her tummy felt tight. "Where is my plant?" she asked. Gran patted her back. "Keep watering," said Gran. "A sprout does not come up right away."

So Olivia watered the pot each day. She watched and waited. On the fifth morning, something green poked up. It was small and curly. "It came!" Olivia shouted. Gran smiled and clapped. Olivia touched one soft leaf, very gently, with one finger.

activity: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
knowledge_domain: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
fact: A blessing before a meal often says thank you for the food.
story:
Ivy sat on the soft grass at the cemetery. Her family had a picnic near Grandpa Joe's stone. The sun was warm and the grass was dry.

Mama held up a basket. "Time for our bread and apples," she said. "First we say our blessing. A blessing before a meal often says thank you for the food."

Ivy did not know the blessing yet. Daddy said the words, but they went too fast. Ivy only caught "thank you for the apples." She frowned. She wanted to say it too.

Then Ivy looked at her apple. She thought about the apple tree. She thought about the sun that made it red. She thought about the farmer who picked it. Now she knew what to say.

"One, two, three," said Ivy. "Thank you for the apple. Thank you for the bread. Thank you for the farmer. Thank you for Grandpa Joe." She took a big bite of the apple. It was sweet and cold.

Daddy gave her a big smile. "You made our blessing longer," he said. Mama clapped her hands, one, two, three.

A little wind moved the grass. The flowers by Grandpa's stone nodded up and down. Ivy waved at them. "Hello, Grandpa Joe," she said. "You are welcome too."

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: Friends playing pretend together can agree on what happens next.
story:
Maverick sat on Grandma's soft rug. He held his toy pig. "Time for bed, pig," he said. He tucked the pig under a little blanket.

Then his cousin Poppy came in. "The pig is sick," said Poppy. "No," said Maverick. "The pig is just sleepy." They both looked at the pig.

"How about a sleepy pig with a sniffle?" said Poppy. "Yes!" said Maverick. He patted the pig gently. Poppy got a tiny toy cup. She held it to the pig's snout. "Drink this," she said. "It will help."

Grandma sat in her big chair nearby. The kettle whistled in the kitchen. The room smelled like warm bread. Grandma gave them each a small cup of milk.

"May the pig have a cookie?" asked Maverick. "That would be very polite," said Grandma, smiling. Poppy swung the pig in a happy dance. "All better!" she said.

Maverick hugged the pig tight. "Night night, pig," he whispered.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
fact: Measuring cups and spoons help cooks put in the right amount of each thing.
story:
Emma was at the campsite with Dad. She wanted to make pancakes for the family. Dad said, "Let's pour the sugar from the bag." Emma tipped the bag. Sugar rushed out. Too much sugar went in the bowl!

Dad helped her pour it back. Then he held up a little cup. "This is a measuring cup," he said. "It helps us put in the right amount." Emma scooped sugar into the cup. She filled it up. She poured it in. Just right!

She did the same with a spoon. One small spoon of salt. Not too much, not too little. Dad cooked the pancakes on the hot grill. Emma stayed back from the sharp edge of the table and watched.

A green frog hopped near the tent. It sat very still. Emma whispered, "Hello, frog."

The pancakes were ready. Emma took a taste. "Yum!" she said. Dad gave her a big hug.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: Eyelashes help keep dust and bits of dirt out of your eyes.
story:
Anna had a little toy robot. It could puff out air. Anna pushed the button. Whirr! Wind touched her face. She heard the whirr with her ears. She felt the wind on her cheeks.

Then Anna saw dust in the air. Some dust flew toward her eyes. She blinked fast. The dust landed on her eyelashes. It did not go in her eyes.

Anna ran to Mama. "What are these little hairs?" she asked. Mama said, "Those are your eyelashes." Anna blinked again. "Eyelashes stopped the dust!" she said. "Did the dust go in?" asked Mama. "No! My eyelashes caught it."

Anna sniffed a snack with her nose. Cookies! She touched one. It was warm. She took a little bite. Yum! "My eyes are happy," said Anna. "No dust, no sad eyes, no tears." Then she pressed the robot button one more time. Whirr, blink, blink!

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: When you play house, each person can pick a role, like the parent or the baby.
story:
Jake wanted to play house with his gray robot toy. His friend Mia came into the playroom. "I want to be the parent," said Mia. "I want to be the parent too," said Jake. They both held the same toy pot. Neither one would let go.

Then Mia had an idea. "We can pick roles," she said. "I will be the parent now. You can be the baby." Jake sat in the little chair like a baby. Mia fed him a pretend bottle. Then Mia patted the robot. "You are the baby's robot," she said.

After that, Mia said, "Now let's switch. You be the parent." Jake stood up tall. He rocked the robot in his arms. He gave the robot a soft blanket. "Time for bed," Jake said in a big parent voice. Mia giggled and clapped her hands.

Then they put all the toys away together. The pot went back on the shelf. The blanket went in the basket. "Same game tomorrow?" asked Mia. Jake nodded and hugged his robot. "You can be the parent first," he said.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
fact: Wet and dry are opposites.
story:
Austin went to the playground with his dad. The sun was hot on his face. He found a big slide and a small slide. He went down the small one. Then he went down the big one. "You were fast on that one," said Dad. Austin saw a boy going slow on a little toy horse. The boy rocked back and forth, back and forth.

Then Austin saw a puddle. He did not go alone. Dad stood right there. Austin jumped in the puddle. Splash! His socks got wet. The water was cold on his toes.

"My socks are all wet," said Austin.

"Wet and dry are opposites," said Dad. He pulled dry socks from the bag. The wet socks went in. The dry socks went on. Austin touched his toes. They were warm again. "Fast, fast, fast," he said, and ran to the swings.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: In pretend play, a cardboard box can become a car, a boat or a house.
story:
Nova went to her friend Milo's house. It was early, right after breakfast. In the playroom, Milo had a big cardboard box.

"I want it to be a car," said Milo. "Vroom, vroom!"

"No, a boat," said Nova. "Row, row!"

They both pulled the box. It tipped over. They both sat down hard.

Milo's mom came in. "Maybe you can take turns," she said.

First it was a car. Milo sat in the box. Nova pushed it a little. "Beep beep!" she said. Then Nova crawled in too. They drove to the kitchen for pretend gas.

Then it was a boat. Nova rowed with a wooden spoon. Milo held a teddy bear. "Teddy is sleepy," said Milo. They rocked the box slow and soft. Teddy closed his eyes.

Then Nova had an idea. "Now let's make it a house," she said. They turned the box on its side. It had a door and a little window.

Teddy peeked out of the window. "Hello!" said Nova, in a tiny bear voice.

The doorbell rang. It was the real mail truck. Nova gasped. "A bus for teddy!" she said. She waved at the window.

"Tomorrow," said Milo, "our box can be a rocket."

"Yes," said Nova. "Zoom, zoom!"

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
fact: When you feel excited, you might want to jump, bounce or shout.
story:
A puppet show was coming to daycare. Liam was so excited. His tummy felt jumpy. His feet wanted to bounce. He bounced and bounced. He wanted to shout, too.

"Look at me!" Liam shouted. He bumped the toy box. Blocks fell out with a noisy crash. Mia began to cry. She felt sad. Liam felt bad. Teacher Amy knelt down. "It's okay," she said softly. She helped Mia pat the blocks back into the box. Liam helped too.

"Waiting is hard," said Teacher Amy. "When you feel excited, you might want to jump, bounce or shout." Liam sat on his hands. He took a big breath. He patted his knees, slow and slow. His feet got still.

The puppet show began. A red dragon danced! Liam clapped and laughed. The dragon landed right on his lap. "Hello, dragon," said Liam.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
fact: Tracing around the bottom of a round cup draws a circle.
story:
Emile ran into art class. He wanted to draw a big sun today. He sat down all alone at the little table. He picked up his yellow crayon. First he drew the sun's rays. Those were easy lines. But the round part was hard. His circle came out wobbly. It looked like a squished egg. He tried again. It was still wobbly. Emile frowned at his paper.

Then he saw Mia. She had a round cup on her paper. She was drawing all around the bottom of it. She lifted the cup up. "Look, a circle!" she said. Emile jumped up. "I want to try that!"

He found a cup too. He held it down on his paper. He drew all around the bottom. He lifted the cup away. There it was, a perfect circle! Emile laughed out loud. He colored the circle yellow. Now his sun had a good round face. He drew a square house next to it. He drew a triangle roof on top. He drew a rectangle door.

"Teacher, look!" said Emile. The teacher took a photo of the sun with her phone. "What a big beautiful sun," she said. "I will play suns all day," said Emile. He grabbed another cup and drew one more circle.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
fact: Only a grown-up gives you medicine, even if it looks like candy.
story:
Eva went to the playground with her grandma. The sun was hot on the slide. The bench in the shade was cold. Eva touched the bench with one finger. "Cold," she said. She stayed close to grandma the whole time.

At the picnic table, Eva saw something shiny. It was a little box with red and white dots inside. The dots looked like candy. Eva wanted to touch them. She counted, "One, two, three dots." Then she remembered. She did not touch. "Grandma, come and see," she called.

Grandma came right away. She looked at the dots. "Only a grown-up gives you medicine," grandma said. "Even if it looks like candy." Grandma picked up the box and put it high in her bag. Eva went back to the slide. She slid down, one, two, three times. "Good watching, Eva," said grandma. Eva held grandma's hand all the way home.

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
fact: Rinsing your brush in water before a new colour keeps the colours clean.
story:
Zoe sat at the paint table at school. She wanted to paint a magic dragon. The dragon would be green, like a shiny leaf.

First she painted the dragon yellow. Then she wanted blue wings. She put her brush in the blue paint. She painted a wing. But the wing was not blue. It was muddy and dark.

Zoe frowned at her dragon. "Your wing looks like mud," she told it politely. The teacher walked by with a cup of water. She set it on the table. Zoe looked at the water. She dipped her brush in. She swished it around. The water turned yellow, then clear again.

Now Zoe put her brush in the blue paint. She painted the other wing. It was bright, clean blue. She gasped. She painted blue over the yellow body. The dragon turned green. Real green. Magic green!

"Look at my green dragon!" Zoe said. She held it up to the window. The sun made the paint shine like jewels. The dragon looked ready to fly. Zoe gave it one more clean green swirl.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
fact: Practicing again and again makes throwing and catching get easier.
story:
Sebastian stood in the backyard. He had a red beanbag. He wanted to throw it into the hoop. The hoop lay on the grass like a circle. He threw the beanbag. It landed far away in the flowers.

Sebastian frowned. He tried again. The beanbag missed the circle again. "I can't do it," he said. His dad was busy raking leaves nearby. "Try one more time," said Dad, soft and kind.

Sebastian picked up the beanbag. He threw it again. It missed. He tried again. And again. Then the beanbag went up, up, and down. It landed right inside the hoop. Sebastian jumped. "It went in!" he said.

Then Dad rolled a big blue ball to him. Sebastian held out both hands. The ball bounced off his fingers. Dad rolled it again. Sebastian missed. But he kept trying, again and again. Soon the ball came right into his arms. He held it tight with both hands. "Look, Dad!" he called. "I caught it!"

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: The counting words always go in the same order: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
story:
Ivy went to the playground on a summer day. She wanted to slide ten times. She loved the slide.

A boy named Sam stood at the bottom. He was counting the swings. "One, two, four," said Sam. His big sister shook her head. "Four does not come next," she said. "The counting words always go in the same order. One, two, three, four." Sam tried again. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" He laughed and clapped.

Ivy was careful as she climbed the slide ladder. She slid down fast. "One!" she said. She slid again. "Two!" She slid and slid. "Three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine..." Her juice cup tipped over. It did not spill, because her mama had closed the lid tight. Ivy slid one more time. "Ten!" she called. "Ten slides!" Sam cheered from the swings. "Now me!" he said. "One, two, three, four..."

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
fact: A plant's roots grow down into the soil.
story:
Olivier went to the garden with Papa. He had tiny carrot seeds in his hand. He wanted to grow big carrots for a snack.

Olivier made a little hole. He dropped a seed in. He patted the soft brown soil on top. "Grow, little seed," he said. Papa gave him a cookie to eat while they waited and watered.

Days went by. Green leaves popped up. But one leaf was not a carrot. "Can I pull it out?" Olivier asked. Papa nodded. Olivier pulled. Out came a weed with long stringy tails. He stared. "What are those wiggly bits?"

"Roots," said Papa. "A plant's roots grow down into the soil."

Olivier looked down at his carrots. "Your roots are under there," he said. He watered the soil. Maybe the roots could feel the wet. A pink worm wiggled by his shoe. Olivier waved. "Hello, worm. Say hi to my roots."

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: Your name written down has the same letters in the same order every time.
story:
Eliana wanted Grandma to read the purple book. But there were so many books. "Which one is mine?" she asked. Grandma pointed to a stack. "One has your name inside," she said.

Eliana opened a book. She turned the pages the right way, front to back. On the first page she saw little black marks. "What are those?" she asked. "Those are words," said Grandma. "They say your name." Eliana looked hard. E, then L, then more letters. "Eliana," she read. Then she saw her name on a birthday card on the table. E, then L, then the same letters again. Same letters, same order, both times!

A tiny ladybug began to crawl across the page. It stopped right on the E. "Even the ladybug likes my name," said Eliana. She ran to the big map on the wall. "Does the map say Eliana too?" Grandma laughed. "No, the map says places." So Eliana pointed to the purple book. "Read this one, Grandma. It has words too." Grandma opened it, and Eliana turned the very first page.

activity: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
knowledge_domain: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
fact: A doctor uses a stethoscope to listen to your heart beating.
story:
Isaac sat in the waiting room with his father. He held his favorite blue truck. Today Isaac was getting a shot. His tummy felt funny about it.

A doctor came in. A tube hung around her neck. "What is that?" Isaac asked. "A stethoscope," said the doctor. "It listens to your heart beating." She put the little ends in Isaac's ears. She put the other end on his chest. Thump, thump! Isaac heard his own heart. It beat fast, like a drum. He took a big breath. The sound got calm and slow.

Then it was shot time. Isaac squeezed his truck. His father held his hand. Quick poke, one tear, all done. "All done, brave boy," said the doctor. She put a bandage on his arm. Isaac pressed his hand to his chest. He could feel his heart go thump, thump. "Still beating," he told his truck. His father picked him up and they walked out. "Ice cream next," his father said.

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
fact: Icy ground is slippery, so people walk slowly and carefully on it.
story:
Elena looked out the window and gasped. Snow! Lots and lots of snow! "No school today," said Mama. "It is a snow day!" Elena put on her boots and her red coat. She ran out to the sidewalk.

Then her boot slid sideways. Whoosh! Elena sat down in the snow. She felt grumpy. She stood up and tried again. She ran, and she fell again. "Why do I keep falling?" she asked. Mama smiled. "The ice is slippery," she said. "Try walking slowly."

Elena took one small step. Then another small step. She did not fall! Slow steps, slow steps, all the way down the street. She let her mittens wave at Mama. At the corner, Dad was scraping ice with a hammer, tap, tap, tap. "Look at me, Dad!" Elena called. "Slow and careful, slow and careful!" She walked all the way to him without one single fall.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: A teacher is the grown-up who looks after and helps the children in a class.
story:
Matteo put on his new shoes. Today was his first day of school. His tummy felt funny. He held Mama's hand all the way.

The classroom was big. Many children ran and played. Matteo hid behind Mama's coat. His foot did not want to move.

A lady with a red sweater came near. "Hello," she said. "I am Miss Ana. I am your teacher. A teacher looks after the children in the class. I help them too."

Matteo peeked out. "Miss Ana?" he said, very small. "Yes, that is me," she said. She waited. She did not rush him.

Matteo let go of the coat. He took one step. Then another. "Hello, Miss Ana," he said. Miss Ana smiled. "Would you like to see the blocks?" Matteo nodded, and he walked with her to the blocks.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: Small toys can roll or slide under furniture like couches and beds.
story:
Jasper had a special red car. He took it to the school playground. Now the car was gone. "Where is my car?" Jasper said. His teacher Miss Ana came close. "We will find it," she said. "Don't worry."

Jasper looked and looked. One look at the sandbox. No car. Two looks at the slide. No car. Three looks at the climbing bars. No car.

Then Jasper saw the little playhouse. It had a small couch and a small bed inside. The car had wheels. Wheels can roll. Jasper got down low. He peeked under the small couch. There it was! The red car had rolled under the couch. Jasper reached in and grabbed it.

Miss Ana smiled. Jasper held the car up high. "Found you!" he said. Then he put a green leaf on top of it, like a little blanket. "Now you can rest."

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: Waiting in line means staying in your place until it is your turn.
story: William wanted the fast red car. Ben had it. Maya wanted it too. Teacher Sam said, "Make a line." William stood by the door. Maya stood behind him. Ben stood behind Maya. "A line means staying in your place until it is your turn," said Sam. William wiggled his feet. He waited. He watched Ben roll the car. Zoom, zoom. Then Maya got her turn. She rolled it fast to the wall. Then it was William's turn. He held the red car. He rolled it far. The car went under the shelf. "I will get it," said Sam. She shut the little door and reached in. She gave the car back. Then it was Ben's turn again. William sat down to wait. Soon Sam called, "Time to wash hands for dinner." William stood up. He said, "My turn again tomorrow!" Ben nodded. "Yes, your turn," said Ben. Then they all ran to wash hands.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
fact: Never look straight at the sun, because it can hurt your eyes.
story:
Florence ran into the backyard. Grandma followed with a pink hat for her.

"Let's play a guessing game," said Grandma. "You have five senses. Guess one!"

" Eyes!" said Florence. She pointed at her eyes.

"Good. Eyes see," said Grandma. "Now look at the flowers."

Florence looked. She saw a pink rose. "My eyes see the rose!" she said.

Then Florence looked up at the sky. She wanted to see the sun. She began to turn her face up to it.

"Stop," said Grandma. She put her hand over Florence's eyes. "Never look straight at the sun. It can hurt your eyes."

Florence blinked. "Okay," she said. "I will not look."

She pointed at her ears. "Ears hear!" she said. Grandma clapped. Florence heard the clap.

"Nose smells," said Florence. She sniffed the rose. "Mmm!"

Then a bee buzzed by. Florence touched a fuzzy leaf. "Hands feel the leaf!" she said.

"One more," said Grandma. "Which body part is left?"

Florence thought. Then she giggled and pointed at her mouth. "Mouth tastes! That was fun!"

Grandma laughed. "All five senses. Now let's go find a snack for that tasting mouth."

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: Sharing means letting someone else use something too.
story:
Connor ran to the big sandbox at the playground. He had the only blue truck there. He pushed it up and down the sand. "Vroom," he said.

Then Mia came. She sat down next to him. She had no truck at all. She watched Connor play. Her hands sat still in the sand.

Connor stopped his truck. He looked at Mia. Then he looked at his truck. He held it out. "You can use it too," he said. "That is sharing."

Mia smiled big. "Thank you," she said. She took the truck and made a long road in the sand. Connor patted the sand flat with his hands. It was hard work, and he patted it again and again.

Then Mia gave the truck back. "Now you," she said. Connor drove it over the new road. One turn for him. One turn for her. The sun was warm. The sand smelled like summer.

Mia asked, "Can we do this again tomorrow?" Connor nodded. "Yes. Come early," he said. "I will bring my truck and two shovels."

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: Teams warm up by running or stretching before a game.
story:
Sophie ran to the soccer field with her team. The coach had a red cone in her hand. "Time to warm up!" said Coach. "What is warm up?" Sophie asked. "We run and we stretch first," said Coach.

Sophie wanted to kick the ball right away. She looked at the gray sky and stomped her little foot. "But I want to play now," she said. Coach smiled a soft smile. "Come run with us, Sophie."

Sophie ran around the cone with her friends. They reached up high and touched their toes. Her legs felt fast and ready. Grandpa waved from the bench by the tree.

The game began. Sophie ran after the ball. Her feet felt quick and strong. She kicked the ball to her friend Mia. Mia kicked it into the net. The team cheered, but nobody fell down or had to cry. Grandpa clapped his hands. Sophie ran to him and hugged his knees. "Grandpa, we warmed up first," she said. "And then we played our best game!"

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: Covering your ears with your hands makes loud sounds quieter.
story:
Olivier was at the doctor's office. He was not scared. He wanted a sticker before they went home. But first, the doctor had to check him.

"I will look in your ears," the doctor said. Olivier saw the little light. He heard it click on. The doctor let him smell a sticker. It smelled like strawberries. At the end, the doctor gave him a sweet taste of medicine. It tasted like cherry.

Then the doctor turned on a loud machine to clean her table. Bzzzzz! It was very loud. Olivier did not like the loud sound. He put his hands over his ears. The loud sound got quiet. His hands made it quiet.

The machine stopped. Olivier took his hands off his ears. He could hear Mommy's voice again.

"Loud is gone," Olivier said.

"Your hands are good helpers," said Mommy.

Olivier got two stickers. He drew a plane on the paper with one, big and blue. They were the last ones in the box, but not too late to get them. On the way out, Olivier touched the soft door. It was warm and smooth.

"Home now," he said, holding Mommy's hand.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
fact: When a family gets home from a trip, they unpack their bags and put things away.
story:
Zayn was four. He was going on a big trip. The whole family rode a ferry across the water. Zayn held the rail with both hands. The wind made his hair flap. The ferry went up and down on the waves. "Look, Mama," said Zayn. "The boat makes the water splash!" The waves rolled and rolled behind them.

On the ferry there was a little cafe. Papa stirred sugar into his tea with a spoon. Zayn drank his milk. Then he played with a tiny packet. Inside was one seed, all alone. "How did a seed get in here?" asked Zayn. Nobody knew. Mama put the seed in her pocket, safe.

At the beach, Zayn ran in the sand. His shoes came off. His feet got sandy and stinky. He giggled and put his shoes back on. Then it was time to go home.

The next day, Mama said, "We unpack our bags now." Zayn opened his little bag. He pulled out his shirt. He pulled out his socks. Then he shook his shoes. Sand fell out onto the floor. "The beach is still in my shoes!" he laughed. Papa laughed too. Zayn put his shirt in the drawer. He put the socks in the basket. The shoes went by the door. His bag was empty at last. "All done," said Zayn, and he clapped his hands.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
fact: Holding your arms out with your hands open gets you ready to catch.
story:
Hannah stood in the big school gym. Her teacher put a small beanbag in her hand. "Throw it in the hoop," said Teacher Joe. Hannah threw it. The beanbag flew past the hoop and landed on the floor. "Oh well," said Hannah. She tried again. This time she threw it slowly. The beanbag went in the hoop. "I did it!" said Hannah.

Then Teacher Joe rolled a big ball to her. The ball hit her legs and stopped. "Why did the ball fall down?" Hannah asked. "My hands were in my pockets." Teacher Joe smiled. "Try holding your arms out," he said. "Keep your hands open."

The ball rolled to Hannah again. Her arms were out. Her hands were open. The big ball went right into her hands. "I caught it!" she shouted. Her friend Ben clapped. "Now me," said Ben. He held his arms out too.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
fact: If you paint on one half of a paper and fold it while the paint is wet, the paint prints onto the other half.
story:
Asher sat at the big craft table at the library. He wanted to make a butterfly. But his butterfly had only one wing, and it looked sad.

Asher painted one wing with red paint. He painted dots too. His tummy felt hungry, but he wanted to finish first. The paint was wet and shiny.

Then Asher folded the paper in half. He pressed it down with his hands. He did not scratch the paint. He opened the paper slowly.

"Wow!" said Asher. The paint had printed on the other half. Now the butterfly had two wings. The wings matched, red with dots on both sides.

"Look, look!" Asher said. A girl named Mia came over. Her butterfly had one wing too. Her face looked sad like his had.

"Fold it," said Asher. "Fold it while the paint is wet." Mia folded her paper. She opened it. Two blue wings, both the same!

"Now we each have a butterfly," said Mia. The librarian smiled and hung them by the window. The sun made the red and blue wings shine like a rainbow.

"Two wings are better than one," said Asher. He clapped his painty hands together.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
fact: A library puts its books on shelves in groups so people can find them.
story:
William sat in his little car seat. "Big world, little car," said Daddy. William looked out the window. He saw one cow. Then two horses. Then a dog on a porch. William tapped the glass. The dog wagged its tail. Tap, tap, wag, wag. William laughed. "Big world, little car," he said.

William had an itchy tag in his shirt. Daddy reached back and fixed it. "All soft now," said Daddy. William cuddled his toy bear. The bear did not fall. William held him tight.

Soon the car stopped. "We are at the library," said Daddy. "I want a book with animals," said William. "Animal books live together on one shelf," said the librarian. "The books are in groups, so we can find them." She pointed. There was a shelf of animal books. There was a shelf of toy books. There was a shelf of food books.

William picked a big book. It had a cow on it. It had a horse on it. It even had the dog. Daddy put the book on the table. William sat on the little chair and turned the pages.

At home, Daddy read to William. "One cow," said Daddy. "Two horses," said William. "Big world, little book," said Daddy. William hugged his bear and tapped the page. The cow in the picture stood still, but William waved anyway. "Hello, cow," he said.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: If you lose something in a busy place, you tell your grown-up instead of going to search by yourself.
story:
Evelyn ran to the park with Dad. She carried her blue bunny in her arms. First they went down the slide. Then they played in the sand. Then they sat on the big rock for a snack.

After the snack, Evelyn looked for bunny. Bunny was gone! She wanted to run far away to look. She took one step, then two steps, then three steps.

Then she stopped. "Dad!" she called. "Bunny is lost. Come look with me." Dad took her hand. "Good job telling me," he said.

They looked together. One, the slide. Two, the sand. Three, the big rock. Evelyn peeked behind the rock. There sat bunny, all sandy and safe.

Evelyn hugged bunny tight. "No more running off alone," she said. Dad smiled. "We find things together."

Then Evelyn put bunny in her pocket, so bunny could not fall. They walked home, counting the trees. One, two, three. Bunny peeked out and saw the blue sky.
